Review: Saw NIN at the Spectrum Center last night, the show was great however the venue is getting increasingly more difficult to visit. Security is jerky and defensive in general, I've seen many bands at the Spectrum Center going all the way back to when it was still Time Warner. I frequently go to concerts and am well versed in venuearena etiquette. That being said, a few years back I purchased a LIVE NATION concert bag, which is basically a small clear rucksack, at a concert in which my already small bag was still too big. Since then, I have taken this 'concert bag' to every show I've been to including ones at the Spectrum Center because it is literally designed to meet venue bag requirements. Last night however, security tried to keep me from entering with my 'concert bag'. The measuring board they were using for bag sizing was 2 centimeters shorter than my bag that was literally designed and sold by the people that sold me the tickets to this concert!!!!! Like... excuse me?!?! I finally convinced them to let me in with it BUT after that I had a Zippo lighter in my bag and they wanted me to throw it away!!!! My concert companion ran it back to the hotel but seriously?!?! Your staff asked me to throw away a 50 lighter!!! One even said 'if you throw that away I am gonna take it'. Evidently they weren't allowing anyone inside with lighters, vapes or even a pack of cigarettes!!! What?!? I understand safety and security rules and regulations, most of which I think are pretty reasonable and it is reassuring no one is allowed in with a knife or weapon BUT what is someone going to do with a cigarette? Are you worried someone is going to set a fire? It is so dumb and the security situation in general is getting ever more draconian. If you're going to be so strict with this type of stuff you need to have a bagcoat check so you don't have to throw away your personal property. How anyone thinks it is reasonable to ask a patron to throw their baglighterwhatever away is beyond me. I will say the lovely girl that scanned our tickets was very pleasant and sweet. The best part of the venue is the fountain Diet Dr. Pepper and free refills, with the price of drinks the refills should be free.

Obviously the ones posting in this thanking the Spectrum Center were involved in the whole process and of course theyd thank them for it, it worked out perfectly in their favor, without regard to anything else. This entire situation was extremely unprofessional. Honestly, legal trouble too. These girls were not employees, and the Spectrum Center walking off of property to hand out wristbands to honor these girls who were holding wristbands for their friends, threatening to remove others from their fan made lists, and going to the Raleigh concert while keeping their place in line in Charlotte is insane. Justin and Daniel were being borderline flirtatious with these girls as well, and you wont get anywhere going to their email since Justin responds back to those emails. Not only was this wildly inappropriate and unprofessional, these girls were laughing in peoples faces, making fun of people, taking turns going to their hotel but then threatening to remove people from their list who werent at their tents the whole time, etc. This is why you do not honor fan made lines and why no where doesnt 99.9 of the time. I hate that I had to be part of this camping problem, because you all let this go down and the only way to get a good spot was to comply with these mean girls who tried to act like they were nice, calm, and professional when people were obviously upset with their behavior. Its also very obvious by you all giving them candy and stuff to post on tik tok is just a ploy for your new arena announcement, its pretty disturbing. Theres better ways to do this, and you all should take some serious pointers from the Heritage Center in Cincinnati. When we went there almost a year ago, they handed out wristbands a day prior to the concert but didnt say what exact time until like an hour before and were partnered with the police to escort campers away that were on and near the property until it was closer to time to hand them out. Once you got your wristbands at Heritage, you got a set time that matched your wristband number to come back the day of the concert to help line people up prior, unlike this venue waiting until exactly 5:30 to actually like people up. Heritage also had Porta Potties for people, water bottles, ice packs etc. This was a huge fumble on your alls part and disgraceful. I hate I had to be part of the camping issue due to your alls negligence and willingness to actually step in and handle the wristbands. Honestly though, the issue wasnt the camping, it was you all allowing random fans to dictate the whole entire general admission line rather than the actual arena. You all need to get a grip.

Review: Every single thing should have been fantastic- entry was easy, staff was communicative and polite, signage was on point and I could find everything I wanted. Ushers were easy to find, helpful, and lovely. I would have had a genuinely amazing experience here- except there was a giant spot light pointed directly at my seat at a very dark show. I dont turn on the over head lights in my house almost ever. Its like someone screaming in my ear. Its abrasive, its horrible, its impossible to ignore. This was exponentially worse than a home overhead light- it was an actual spotlight! In a dark concert! I also do not like being the center of attention, so knowing that my every move is highlighted to disturb everyone around me completely takes any enjoyment of the show Im watching. I had wanted to see two of the bands playing for decades. I was so excited to see them, and though my seats werent good, it cost me a lot to be there. We drove three hours to get to the show. I asked an usher for help- though polite, his answer was essentially its sold out, get over it. I also work at a performing arts venue- this is unacceptable. At no point when I booked was I alerted that there would be a spot light on my seat. We ended up having to leave the show while the main band was still on because I had a migraine from this light. Please be aware if you book an aisle seat, you might have a spot light uncomfortably on you. Probably just see whatever act you want to see in a different city and dont go to this venue.

Review: We have been going to the spectrum Center for years. I was previously a partial season ticket holder for the Charlotte Hornets. I gave them up due to the expenses that come with traveling to Charlotte from Winston Salem. My kids took me yesterday for the Knicks game as a Birthday gift. After being on an u organized and chaotic line for half hour, we get to the front and a security lady comes out of nowhere and tells my wife she cant go in with her CLEAR bag. I advised her we purchased it the previous year in the arena. She said, New owners, new rules in a nasty tone. The bag was about 3 inches bigger than the 7 they now admit, Mind you, its clear and was only 14 full. Then her and another security guard said get out of the line and go to the back after you put your bag in the car. They were doing this to a lot of people, even one with a stroller. They were not professional at all. Super Nasty! The worse part was that inside we saw bigger SOLID pocketbooks and bags!!!! Luckily it was a good game and I cooled down. The new colors on the basketball floor are cool. The overhead is crystal clear. Staff inside was nice. Prices are still high for food and drinks, add tickets and parking and its becoming a rich mans night out. We had fun and our NY Knicks won! Update: Its nice to come out here once in a while to catch a game but it gets expensive. Between tickets and parking, its become a rich mans sport, just like every other sport. My biggest complain is the food quality. They have switched over to self serve kiosks where you tap your card and grab and go. The food does not feel fresh and could be sitting quite a bit of time. They also have someone making you take the cap off your drinks and throwing them out. This becomes a hassle to carry and spill and sodas go flat quickly. We got the Chicken strips and waffle fries and they were worse than what you would get at a gas station. The nachos come in a small bag with a sealed cold cheese sauce, just nasty! Not a lot of nachos in the bag and no option of jalapeños or chili or HOT cheese! Just not worth it for the money you pay. Better off eating ahead or after the games. I would love to see more affordable t shirts or value worthy gifts for everyone, not just the people with money to spare. Would love to come to more games but 1 or 2 a year is my limit. I can only afford nosebleeds and for that I might as well stay in the comfort of my home.

The only bad part was seating we had floor seats was so close to each other not only side by side but the chairs in front of us barely left room for people to walk by. Me and the wife wanted to dance around but could barely move. I'm not going to knock any stars off for that miniscule problem. JTs performance made up for that!

The venue itself is great, offering a comfortable and enjoyable experience for various events. However, the overall environment can be disappointing due to the crowds it attracts. Unfortunately, this often leads to the area becoming trashy and dirty, and potentially dangerous detracting from the otherwise excellent facilities. While the Spectrum Center has potential, the issues with ambiance and the behavior of some attendees impact the overall experience. Improved crowd management and maintenance could make it a superior venue.
